question: Where are the hot and cold spots of the first nonconstant Neumann mode?
idea: The manuscript studies the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a smooth bounded planar domain with no holes. It claims every corresponding nonzero eigenfunction has no critical point in the interior, so its maximum and minimum lie on the boundary. This is not a claim about every possible temperature profile or eigenmode.
why: The study of equations that describe how quantities vary across space and time, such as waves, fluids, and heat.

exactClaim: Proves a strict form of Burdzy's simply connected hot spots conjecture. On every smooth bounded simply connected planar domain, each nonzero eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has no interior critical point, so all global extrema lie on the boundary. Eigenvalue multiplicity is allowed. )
